rejectionGroups.reason: These hanger-only shirts provide no adult fit proof and use large geometric contrast panels that read as dated supplier color blocking rather than clean modern tailoring.
The product-only floral shirt has a shiny synthetic-looking surface and oversized blurred blossoms, with no shoulder, torso or hem proof for a controlled adult fit.
The basic gingham shirt is product-only, carries a visible lower-placket label and adds another black or gray checked role already covered by stronger on-body options.
Both blue gradient shirts use an artificial white-to-dark fade that looks dated and difficult to coordinate; the hanger-only images also do not prove adult fit.
These separate supplier identities use the same or near-identical blue-and-white plaid presentation with an oversized contrast flap pocket, so accepting either would create an obvious visual repeat.
These product-only brown plaids provide no adult fit proof and repeat dark, conventional checks without a cleaner construction or useful modern color advantage.

The regular-fit plaid is acceptable in isolation, but both muted blue and green-grid roles are already represented by visually approved shirts, so it would add another near-repeat rather than a real wardrobe gap.
These near-duplicate fleece-lined plaid shirts are bulky winter hybrids with conspicuous tan lining, hanger-only proof and insufficiently distinct styling to justify two more neutral checked layers.
The active-short image is tightly cropped at the waist and upper thigh, so it does not prove full length, leg opening or complete silhouette; black and gray also repeat crowded activewear roles.
These long bottoms are visibly over-wide or heavily pooled at the shoe, reproducing the baggy and puddled silhouette specifically excluded from the men’s styling brief.
The lightweight shorts are long and narrow through the leg and repeat already approved white, khaki and neutral casual-short roles without a stronger modern shape.
These all-black joggers use tight cuffs, long contrast drawcords, stripes or extra trim and read as dated supplier gymwear rather than clean modern active bottoms.
The product-only navy drawstring trouser has no rise, seat, thigh or shoe-break proof, while the oversized white rope cord dominates an otherwise generic silhouette.
The very short gym silhouette carries a conspicuous GYMBULL waistband mark and repeats active-short roles already represented by cleaner, less logo-led pieces.
The double-layer camo compression short combines a visible supplier logo, busy print and bulky mesh overlay, making it unsuitable for the clean premium activewear direction.
The product-only parka is a generic technical shape with SPORTMENS chest text, sleeve patch and multiple decorative zipper details rather than a clean versatile winter layer.

These product-only stand-collar puffers are visually near-duplicate basics, and the approved inventory already contains multiple beige, green, blue and light puffer roles with stronger differentiation.
The hooded shell uses stark chevrons, contrast cargo pockets, hanging tabs and multiple drawcord details, creating a busy utility look without adult fit proof.
The tactical softshell is a generic dark outdoor jacket with small contrast zipper pulls and no on-body evidence for shoulder, torso or hem proportions.
These heavy parkas use dated multi-pocket military construction, faux-fur or fleece bulk, sleeve patches and excessive trim, producing an older supplier look rather than modern Zara-led outerwear.
The minimal shell is clean, but its product-only khaki, white and navy variants repeat windbreaker roles already approved and do not add new on-body fit evidence.
The color-block windbreaker is visibly wrinkled, uses a conspicuous white chest zipper and has no adult fit proof; the purple recolor intensifies the cheap technical appearance.
The camouflage faux-leather jacket combines glossy synthetic camo, a sweatshirt hood and multiple angled zippers into a dated, costume-like outerwear piece.
